topic: Civil and Guidance Stream Triage — LAB, PBSG Legal Guidance
user_query: Applicant has a civil matter (contract, employment, property, estate, personal injury, neighbour), or simply wishes to get legal guidance before deciding whether to engage a lawyer / apply for legal representation. How do I triage this?
variations: Applicant needs help with employment / wage claim.
Applicant has an estate / probate matter.
Applicant has a personal injury claim.
Applicant wants to understand their legal options before engaging a lawyer.
Applicant is unsure whether they need a lawyer and is seeking guidance.
Applicant wants preliminary legal advice before applying for legal representation.
Applicant wants to assess whether their situation warrants legal representation.
Applicant is seeking legal guidance before deciding on next steps.
part_a_general_info: The Civil and Guidance Stream is the broadest. PBSG generally does NOT have a civil representation scheme. The typical pathway is: (a) Legal Aid Bureau (LAB) for SGC/PR representation; (b) PBSG for guidance; (c) private counsel where neither applies. However, there can be discretion applied by PSBG Staff. If a matter appears exceptional but is not eligible for LAB representation, escalate to PBSG Staff instead of rejecting. LAB (representation) LAB is the government's legal aid office and should be the first port of call for low-income SGC/PR seeking representation for civil and family proceedings. LAB eligibility: • Applicant is a SGC/PR residing in Singapore, or citizens or residents of contracting states who are involved in applications under the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction. • Applicant’s case falls within LAB’s case types (refer to GEN3-I14 — Information Card — Legal Aid Bureau) • Applicant meets LAB’s means test (https://lab.mlaw.gov.sg/legal-services/taking-the-means-test/), financial documents will need to be submitted upon application. • Applicant passes merits test (legal assessment on whether the case warrants representation, this will be done by LAB, intern/volunteer taking triaging call is NOT to reject based on their own assessment, no matter how unmeritorious the case appears to be). Low-income Singapore Citizens / PRs certain that they wish to seek legal representation should be advised to apply to the LAB FIRST for legal aid. Only if LAB is unable to assist, does PBSG become the primary route for SGC/PR. PBSG may be able to provide legal guidance and assess suitability for any further assistance, such as representation, on an exceptional basis. LAB can provide legal advice when processing the legal aid application. PBSG (guidance) • Legal Clinics (guidance): Free 20-minute legal consultations. For low to median-income individuals (regardless of nationality). • There are specialised clinics for various communities and needs, such as clinics for vulnerable individuals, same or next-working day clinics for urgent cases, Syariah law matters, clinics for transnational families, clinics for migrant workers, clinics for individuals with invisible disabilities and their caregivers, clinics for youths, and clinics for artists. These will be triaged by either GEN3-T06 (Urgent Matter), GEN3-T13 (Vulnerable Applicant), or PBSG Staff upon an application for legal clinics. You do NOT need to triage these at this stage or explain these options to the applicant. These options are only flagged here for information, in case the applicant has read about these options in the media and is asking about them. Always listen for urgency cues and vulnerability cues while running these questions. If either surface, cross-reference GEN3-T06 (Urgent Matter) and GEN3-T13 (Vulnerable Applicant) concurrently — do not wait to finish the triage.
triage_questions: Q1: Is the applicant a Singapore Citizen or PR?
Q2 (SGC/PR path): Is the applicant seeking representation (a lawyer to act for them) or guidance (initial advice)?
Q3 (Representation, SGC/PR): Has the applicant applied to the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB)?

Q4 (Means): Is the applicant's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$5,000, does the applicant have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the applicant stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?

Q4A (if Q4 = No): Is the applicant marginally outside the means criteria (meets at least one criterion or has exceptional circumstances), or clearly outside all criteria with no exceptional circumstances?
branching_logic: Q1: Is the applicant a Singapore Citizen or PR?
If Q1 = Yes → Proceed to Q2
If Q1 = No (foreigner) → Proceed to Q4
If Q1 = Not Sure → Clarify nationality/residency status; if still unclear, Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
Q2 (SGC/PR path): Is the applicant seeking representation (a lawyer to act for them) or guidance (initial advice)?
If Q2 = Representation → Proceed to Q3
If Q2 = Guidance → Proceed to Q4

If Q2 = Not Sure / Both → Describe both (including that LAB can provide guidance as part of their application for representation but this is subject to LAB’s means test i.e. for low-income individuals, and applicant will likely need to attend in-person at their HQ or a ServiceSG centre (http://life.gov.sg/services-tools/book-virtual-appointment-minlaw); on the other hand, PBSG provides guidance to low to median-income individuals and can conduct sessions either in-person at Central, North East, North West, South East, South West CDC, or virtually through Zoom with applicant dialling in from a conducive location of their choice); if still undecided → Proceed to Q4
Q3 (Representation, SGC/PR): Has the applicant applied to the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB)?
If Q3 = No → Route B (Refer to LAB)
If Q3 = Yes, LAB unable to assist → Proceed to Q4
If Q3 = Yes, LAB able to assist or Not Sure → Route B.

Q4 (Means): Is the applicant's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$5,000, does the applicant have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the applicant stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?
(PCHI = total monthly household income ÷ number of persons in household, including the applicant and all dependants.)
If Q4 = Yes (all within thresholds) → Route A (Legal Clinic)
If Q4 = No → Ask Q4A before routing.

Q4A (if Q4 = No): Is the applicant marginally outside the means criteria (meets at least one criterion or has exceptional circumstances), or clearly outside all criteria with no exceptional circumstances?
If Q4A = Marginal / exceptional circumstances → Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
If Q4A = Clearly outside all criteria with no exceptional circumstances → Route D (Reject and Share Self-Help Resources)
If Q4A = Not Sure → Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
If Q4 = Not Sure → Walk through the thresholds; if still unclear, take down figures and proceed to Route C (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
routing: Route D (Reject and Share Self-Help Resources):
guardrail: • Under s 33 of the Legal Profession Act 1966, only qualified, practising lawyers may give legal advice. You must NEVER: (a) interpret a legal document for the applicant; (b) apply the law to the applicant's facts; (c) predict the outcome of a case; (d) tell the applicant what they should do legally. • You MAY: (a) confirm scheme eligibility against objective criteria; (b) read out scheme descriptions verbatim; (c) explain PBSG hotline operations; (d) take down particulars and escalate to PBSG Staff. • If the applicant insists on legal advice, respond: “I’m an intern/volunteer and I’m not able to give legal advice. What I can do is help you find the right legal help avenue or direct you to a qualified lawyer.” • If in doubt at any point — escalate to PBSG Staff. • Protect applicant confidentiality. Do not discuss the applicant outside the hotline context. Do not retain personal data on personal devices and/or beyond the PBSG volunteering period.
